target.title: fix(voice-call): fail-closed media-stream auth for non-Twilio providers
target.body:
Closes #102837

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the voice-call media-stream WebSocket endpoint (`/voice/stream`) accepts an unauthenticated `start` frame for non-Twilio providers (Plivo, Telnyx). Anyone who knows a live provider call ID — leaked via a log line, status callback, or prior participation — can connect a WebSocket, inject forged audio into the agent pipeline, and receive the agent's outbound audio.

Only the Twilio provider path enforced the signed per-call stream token. This is the residual half of the previously reported authentication gap (#7001) which was closed for Twilio only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `shouldAcceptStream` callback in `VoiceCallWebhookServer.initializeMediaStreaming` (`webhook.ts:363`) used a hardcoded `this.provider.name === "twilio"` branch to gate token validation, and fell through to `return true` for every other provider. This made the media-stream endpoint permissive for any non-Twilio provider with an active call.

The fix:

1. **`VoiceCallProvider` interface** (`base.ts`) — Declares an optional `isValidStreamToken?(callId, token)` method so any provider can plug in its own per-call credential verification.

2. **`shouldAcceptStream` callback** (`webhook.ts:363`) — Replaces the Twilio-only check with a fail-closed dispatch: if the active provider exposes `isValidStreamToken`, it is called; if not, the stream is **rejected**. Previously the default was `return true` (accept).

Non-goal: This PR does not add per-call stream token generation or validation to Plivo or Telnyx. Telnyx already uses the separate realtime handler path (`realtime-handler.ts`) with its own `consumeStreamToken` UUID-based authentication. Plivo media-stream support can be added with provider-owned credential logic in a follow-up.

## User Impact

Before: A `start` frame with any active call ID and no token was accepted for Plivo or Telnyx media streams. After: the media-stream endpoint **rejects** start frames for providers that have not implemented per-call stream token validation. Twilio deployments are unaffected — existing `isValidStreamToken` logic continues to work. Operators of non-Twilio media-stream deployments must now implement `isValidStreamToken` on their provider before `/voice/stream` connections are accepted; this is the correct secure default.

## Evidence

- **Root cause confirmed**: Source-level reproduction at `extensions/voice-call/src/webhook.ts:363` — Twilio-only token check with fall-through to `return true` for any other provider. Codex review confidence: 0.87.

- **Tests pass** (4 suites, 88 tests):
  - `media-stream.test.ts` — 22 passed
  - `webhook.test.ts` — 46 passed
  - `telnyx.test.ts` — 16 passed
  - `plivo.test.ts` — 4 passed

- **Before/after logic**: The `shouldAcceptStream` callback now rejects non-Twilio provider streams with a warning log including the provider name and call ID, matching the expected fail-closed behavior described in #102837.

---

This PR is AI-assisted. Analysis, implementation, and testing were performed using opencode with review by the author.
